meta.policy: Every entry is an official federal, state, county, municipal, or statutory regional agency source verified directly on 2026-11-26. No commercial brokers, blogs, or unverified aggregators.

sources.agency: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS)
sources.title: Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale, CA — Economy at a Glance (Oct 2026 prelim; extracted 2026-11-20)
sources.notes: NSA unemployment 4.6% (Oct 2026 prelim), total nonfarm 4,662.8k (+0.9% YoY), Leisure & Hospitality 548.0k (+2.0% YoY), LA CPI-U 360.965 (Oct 2026) / 358.725 (+3.7% YoY Sep 2026).

sources.agency: California Employment Development Department (EDD)
sources.title: Los Angeles County Monthly Labor Force & Industry Employment Report (Oct 2026 prelim, March 2025 benchmark)
sources.notes: SA unemployment 4.6% (down from 4.8% rev Sep 2026; CA SA 5.0%, US SA 4.1%). Food Services & Drinking Places 395,000 (+1.9% YoY); Limited-Service Restaurants 193,200 (+1.6% YoY).

sources.agency: California Department of Finance (DOF)
sources.title: E-1 Cities, Counties, and the State Population and Housing Estimates (Jan 1, 2026 Press Release, May 1, 2026)
sources.notes: CA pop 39,592,978 (-0.1% YoY); LA County 9,837,286 (-0.6% YoY, -64,000 persons); City of LA 3,806,201 (-0.9% YoY); 11,160 units lost to Eaton & Palisades fires; LA County added +11,260 net housing units (62.7% multi-family).

sources.agency: U.S. Census Bureau — Population Estimates Program (via FRED)

sources.agency: U.S. Census Bureau — SAIPE (via FRED)
sources.title: Estimate of Median Household Income for Los Angeles County, CA (Series MHICA06037A052NCEN, 1989–2024)
sources.notes: 2024 county median household income $90,757 (+4.92% YoY vs 2023 $86,499; +53.71% nominal since 2015 $59,045). County proxy only; cannot substitute for parcel trade-area tracts.

sources.agency: California Department of Education (CDE)
sources.title: Los Angeles Unified School District Profile (CDS 19-64733-0000000, School Year 2025–26)
sources.notes: SY 2025–26 total enrollment 497,105; English Learners 81,328 (16.4%). District-wide context only; local feeder-school check requires private parcel coordinates.

sources.agency: California Department of Transportation (Caltrans)
sources.title: Traffic Census Program — State Highway AADT & Truck Volumes (through 2024)
sources.notes: State Highway System volumes published annually through 2024. Explicitly directs users to city/county Traffic Engineering for municipal surface-street counts.

sources.agency: Los Angeles Department of Transportation (LADOT)
sources.title: LADOT Traffic Counts Program & NavigateLA Data Repository
sources.notes: Stores surface-street ADT, turning movement, and bike/pedestrian counts on NavigateLA (dating to early 1990s). LADOT TAG guidelines require counts <= 2 years old for studies.

sources.agency: Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)
sources.title: Connect SoCal 2024: Demographics and Growth Forecast Technical Report (April 2024)
sources.notes: Six-county SCAG region population 18.83M (2019) -> 20.91M (2050, +11.1%); LA County employment 5.03M -> 5.46M; household growth outpaces population growth as household size falls.

sources.agency: Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)
sources.title: Technical Working Group Agenda Packet — CARB Evaluation of Connect SoCal 2024 & 2050 Draft (Nov 20, 2025)
sources.notes: Discussion draft highlights downward demographic revision risk: LA County population 9.8M (2024) -> 9.3M (2050, -5%) while households still grow 3.5M -> 3.7M (+6%).

sources.agency: California Department of Industrial Relations (DIR / DLSE)
sources.title: Fast Food Minimum Wage FAQ (AB 1228, Labor Code §1474–1476) & IWC Wage Order 7 (Rev. 11/2025)
sources.notes: Confirms $20.00/hr fast-food minimum wage effective Apr 1, 2024 for limited-service chains with 60+ U.S. units (incl. franchisees). Companion IWC Order 7 (Rev. 11/2025) confirms $16.90/hr CA general minimum wage eff. Jan 1, 2026.

sources.agency: City of Los Angeles — Office of Wage Standards (BCA)
sources.title: Los Angeles Minimum Wage Ordinance Schedule (Effective July 1, 2026)
sources.notes: General City of LA minimum wage $18.42/hr eff. July 1, 2026 (up from $17.87 in 2025, $17.28 in 2024, $16.78 in 2023; CPI-W indexed). Fast-food operators must pay the higher $20.00/hr AB 1228 floor.

sources.agency: Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
sources.title: Revenue Procedure 2025-32 — 2026 Inflation-Adjusted Tax Items (Brackets & §1(h) Capital Gains)
sources.notes: 2026 Federal LTCG 20% thresholds: MFJ > $613,700; Single > $545,500; HOH > $579,600; MFS > $306,850; Estates/Trusts > $16,250 (0% up to $98,900 MFJ / $49,450 Single).

sources.agency: Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
sources.title: Topic No. 409 — Capital Gains and Losses (Unrecaptured Section 1250 Gain 25% Ceiling)
sources.notes: Unrecaptured Section 1250 real-property straight-line depreciation gain taxed up to 25% maximum federal rate; remaining long-term gain at 0%/15%/20%.

sources.agency: Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
sources.title: Topic No. 559 — Net Investment Income Tax (3.8% NIIT, IRC §1411)
sources.notes: 3.8% surtax on lesser of NII or MAGI excess over $250,000 (MFJ), $200,000 (Single/HOH), $125,000 (MFS) — unindexed; Estates/Trusts threshold equals top bracket ($16,000 in 2026).

sources.agency: Internal Revenue Service (IRS)
sources.title: 2026 Instructions for Form 8824 — Like-Kind Exchanges (IRC §1031)
sources.notes: Real property held for business/investment only (post-2017); strict 45-day written identification & 180-day (or return due date) replacement receipt deadlines; boot taxed.

sources.agency: California Franchise Tax Board (FTB)
sources.title: FTB Tax News October 2026 — 2026 California Personal Income Tax Rate Schedules & P.L. 119-21 Summary
sources.notes: 2026 CA brackets 1%–12.30% (top 12.30% over $768,213 Single/MFS, $1,536,426 MFJ, $1,044,771 HOH). Capital gains taxed as ordinary income. Companion FTB federal summary confirms $15M federal estate exclusion (P.L. 119-21).

sources.agency: California Franchise Tax Board (FTB)
sources.title: 2026 Instructions for Form 540-ES — Behavioral Health Services Tax (1% > $1,000,000) & Pub 1016 / Form 3840
sources.notes: 1.00% Behavioral Health Services Tax (formerly Mental Health Services Tax) on CA taxable income > $1,000,000 (all filing statuses) -> 13.30% combined top CA rate. FTB Pub 1016 (Rev. 02/2026) mandates annual Form 3840 reporting/clawback on out-of-state §1031 exchanges.

sources.agency: California State Board of Equalization (BOE) & LA County Assessor
sources.title: Publication 29 (Prop 13 Property Tax Overview) & LA County Assessor Decline-in-Value (Prop 8) 2026 Filing Window
sources.notes: Prop 13: 1% base rate + voter bonds, max 2%/yr inflation cap, reassessed at market value on change in ownership (BOE Pub 29). LA County Prop 8 Decline-in-Value (RP-87) window for 2026–27 closes November 30, 2026 (4 days from 2026-11-26).

sources.agency: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance & LA County Registrar-Recorder (lavote.gov)
sources.title: Real Property Transfer Tax & Measure ULA FAQ — Thresholds Effective July 1, 2026
sources.notes: Effective after June 30, 2026: City Base $2.25/$500 (0.45%) + ULA 4.0% (> $5,400,000 to < $10,900,000) or 5.5% (>= $10,900,000). Confirmed by LA County RR/CC (lavote.gov) plus County DTT $0.55/$500 ($1.10/$1,000 = 0.11%) -> combined 0.56% / 4.56% / 6.06% inside City of LA.

sources.agency: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS)
sources.title: FDSN Earthquake Event Count API (M>=4.5 within 50 km of Central LA, 1990-01-01 to 2026-11-26) & ASCE 7-22 Design Maps
sources.notes: Direct API query returned count = 28 M>=4.5 earthquakes within 50 km of Central LA (34.0522, -118.2437) since 1990. Site-specific ASCE 7-22 spectral parameters require private parcel coordinates.

sources.agency: California Geological Survey (CGS)
sources.title: EQ Zapp — California Earthquake Hazards Zone Application (Alquist-Priolo Fault, Liquefaction & Landslide Zones)
sources.notes: Official statutory mapping tool for Alquist-Priolo fault rupture, liquefaction, and earthquake-induced landslide zones (PRC Div. 2 Ch. 7.5 & 7.8). Must be run privately on parcel coordinates.

sources.agency: Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA — OpenFEMA v2 & NFHL)
sources.title: OpenFEMA Disaster Declarations Summaries — Los Angeles County (FIPS 06037) & National Flood Hazard Layer
sources.notes: 88 total LA County federal disaster declarations on record (refreshed 2026-11-13), incl. DR-4856-CA (Jan 2025 Eaton/Palisades wildfires), FM-5605 (Aug 2025 Canyon Fire), and 2023–2024 severe storm/flood disasters (DR-4683, DR-4699, DR-4769). Flood zone requires private NFHL/MSC parcel check.

sources.agency: CAL FIRE (OSFM) & California Department of Insurance (CDI)
sources.title: Fire Hazard Severity Zones (2025 LRA / 2026 SRA Update) & CDI Sustainable Insurance Strategy / FAIR Plan Order 2026-2
sources.notes: CAL FIRE rolled out 2025 LRA FHSZ maps across all counties (Feb–Mar 2025) and opened 2026 SRA comment window (Nov 9, 2026–Jan 8, 2027). CDI Order 2026-2 & Release 052-2025 confirm FAIR Plan commercial limits expanded to $20M/bldg ($100M/location) eff. July 26, 2025, sunsetting Dec 31, 2028, plus 85% voluntary-market write mandate for catastrophe-model insurers.
